Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that wraps up the second T20I, where India delivered another impressive performance to seal the series with one match still to play. This victory marks India's 16th consecutive T20I series win at home. With the series secured, we could see some of the bench players getting a chance in the final game. As for Bangladesh, they are still searching for their first win on this tour of India across formats and will be eager to finish on a high, particularly with Mahmudullah set to retire after this series. The third and final T20I will take place at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad on Saturday, October 12th. The first ball will be bowled at 1.30 pm GMT, but make sure to join us well ahead of time for all the exciting build-up to the match. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Nitish Kumar Reddy is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his all-round showing - 74 (34) with the bat and 2 for 23 with the ball. He says that it feels great to contribute to the team and wants to enjoy this moment. Says that he should thank the captain and the coach for giving him the license to play his natural game. Tells that he took his time initially, but after that No Ball everything went his way. Shares that it feels great to play for the Indian team and hopes he can contribute more in future games.

Suryakumar Yadav, the victorious Indian skipper says he wanted a tough situation to see how the middle order performs and he is absolutely pleased with the way they played. Talks about the message to be loud and clear for the players to go out and express themselves and play freely. Mentions that he wanted to try to give all the bowlers a go to see what they had to offer. Says it was Nitish's day and he wanted him to go out and bowl with the new ball.

The captain of Bangladesh, Najmul Hossain Shanto says that they made the same mistakes which they did during the first game and need to improve. Feels that it was a good decision to bowl first and they started well but could not execute their plans afterwards. Reckons that as batters, they need to take responsibility and it is important to believe that once you get in, you can get a big score. Mentions that not picking wickets during the middle phase hurt them.
Time for the presentation ceremony...

Rinku Singh is down for a quick chat. He says he backs himself at tough times to keep things calm and believes in himself. Adds that he has practised a lot to bat the way he does and keeps talking to MS Dhoni for his input which helps. Mentions that his talk with Nitish was just to stitch a partnership and make the most of any bad balls that came their way which all started flowing after that No ball went for a six.

Earlier in the game, considering the dew factor, Najmul Hossain Shanto opted to bowl first. Right from the first over, it was clear that this wasn’t a typical Delhi batting paradise, with inconsistent bounce and balls holding up in the surface. After losing their top three within the Powerplay, a 108-run partnership between Nitish Kumar Reddy and Rinku Singh rescued the hosts from trouble. Nitish started cautiously but shifted gears smoothly as the innings progressed. The Bangladeshi spinners also faltered several times with their lines and lengths during the middle overs, further aiding the duo's recovery. Cameos from Hardik Pandya and Riyan Parag propelled India to 221. For Bangladesh, their pacers excelled with Taskin Ahmed being the pick of the bowlers but the spin duo of Mehidy Hasan and Rishad Hossain went for a combined total of 101 runs from their 7 overs.

In most cases, a strong Powerplay is imperative for the chasing side when chasing totals in excess of 200. Unfortunately for the visitors, this did not materialize, as they lost three wickets within the Powerplay. Consequently, they were left playing catch-up for the remainder of their innings. They struggled to build any substantial partnerships as India consistently chipped away at their wickets. Every bowler Suryakumar Yadav turned to, delivered for the side, with seven bowlers used throughout the night, and each one claiming at least one wicket. Bangladesh never found their rhythm in the chase, and with the Delhi surface not being its usual batting-friendly self, the balls stopping and holding up only added to their difficulties.

A comprehensive win for India to put the series to bed! Though they were pushed into a corner early on with the bat, they managed to find a way back and were never under pressure with the ball. A win by 86 runs marks India's biggest win in terms of runs against Bangladesh in T20I cricket. As for Bangladesh, they started well with the ball but will rue the missed opportunity of letting India off the hook after reducing them to 41/3, allowing them to recover and reach a total of 221.

The fielder from deep backward point charges to his left, collects the ball and throws it back to the keeper, Sanju Samson at the striker's end. Mehidy Hasan is quick across the second run and throws a full stretched dive to make his ground.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Varun Chakaravarthy to Mehidy Hasan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Straight and full, on middle, Mahmudullah makes a good block straight to the bowler. Just the three runs and a wicket of Abhishek Sharma's first over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Abhishek Sharma to Mahmudullah, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mahmudullah comes out to bat now with Bangladesh in all sorts of trouble. The veteran all-rounder will be retiring from T20Is at the end of this series and his side needs him to bail them out here.

OUT! CHOPPED BACK ONTO THE STUMPS! Every bowling change seems to be working wonders for Suryakumar Yadav! Abhishek Sharma gets his first and Bangladesh are in deep trouble. Bowls the arm-ball fuller in length just around off, Towhid Hridoy looks to drag the whip across to the leg side. Gets an inside edge that goes back to rattle the stumps. Bangladesh are now 46/4, needing 176 runs from 79 balls.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Abhishek Sharma to Towhid Hridoy, OUT! b Abhishek Sharma.

Commentary.Commentary: Fired in at the pads, Mehidy Hasan clips it to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Abhishek Sharma to Mehidy Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Almost chipped back to the bowler. Abhishek Sharma gives the ball air and keeps it full on middle, Mehidy Hasan looks to tuck it across but closes the bat face a bit too early. Gets a leading edge that falls short of the diving Abhishek Sharma to his front.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Abhishek Sharma to Mehidy Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: And again, keeps it full and on middle and leg, Towhid Hridoy flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Abhishek Sharma to Towhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, full and on middle, Mehidy Hasan pushes it to long on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Abhishek Sharma to Mehidy Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A loud appeal for LBW but the umpire shakes his head. After a long chat, Suryakumar Yadav sends it upstairs. This is quicker too, angling in on middle and leg, Towhid Hridoy goes on the back foot to work it away but gets beaten on the inside edge back onto the pads. The replay however rolls back on and the UltraEdge shows a spike as the ball passes the bat. The on-field call of NOT OUT stays and India lose a review.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Is that out? Varun Chakaravarthy looks convinced and after a chat, Suryakumar Yadav has sent it upstairs for an LBW review. The first replay shows a deflection and there could be an inside edge. Yes, the UltraEdge shows a spike as the ball is next to the bat.
Pushed through quicker and fuller, on middle and leg, Towhid Hridoy taps it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fired in, quicker and fuller, on middle, Towhid Hridoy hops back and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps it short and on middle, Mehidy Hasan hangs back and cuts it to short third where Mayank Yadav dives to his right and keeps it down to one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Varun Chakaravarthy to Mehidy Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A tad shorter and on off, Mehidy Hasan pushes it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Varun Chakaravarthy to Mehidy Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mehidy Hasan walks in at number 5.

OUT! TIMBER! Varun Chakaravarthy makes an immediate impact! Bangladesh slip further down and lose Litton Das for 14 (11). Litton Das will be livid with himself for that shot selection. Varun Chakaravarthy bowls this straight on with the arm, on middle, angling in, the ball keeps a bit low off the surface as well. Litton Das sets himself for the swipe across the line but gets done in by the slowness of the delivery. It zips under his bat and knocks the middle stump off the ground.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Varun Chakaravarthy to Litton Das, OUT! b Varun Chakaravarthy.

Commentary.Commentary: 'Catch it' is the call but it goes on the bounce! Sundar slows it up and bowls it on a nagging length, on off, Litton Das looks to go down town but ends up hitting it flat towards long on for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Washington Sundar to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is fired in, shorter and quicker, on off, Litton Das punches it from the crease to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Washington Sundar to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed through, fuller and on off, Towhid Hridoy eases the drive to wide long on and gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Washington Sundar to Towhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Towhid Hridoy walks out to bat at number 4 for Bangladesh.

OUT! TAKEN! The simplest of catches for Hardik Pandya. Washington Sundar strikes in his first over. A big blow to Bangladesh as their skipper departs for just 11. Speared in from around the wicket by Sundar, on middle and leg. Najmul Hossain Shanto sees the mid off inside the circle and tries to go over him. He fails to create the desired room and ends up dragging it down towards long on. It goes straight down the throat of long on where Hardik Pandya takes it near his waist.
Commentary.Howout: c Hardik Pandya b Washington Sundar
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Washington Sundar to Najmul Hossain Shanto, OUT! c Hardik Pandya b Washington Sundar.

Commentary.Commentary: This goes on with the arm, full and around off, Litton Das knocks it down to long on and crosses over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Washington Sundar to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Darted in straight away by Sundar from around the wicket, full and on middle, Najmul Hossain Shanto sweeps it to deep square leg and gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Washington Sundar to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: First signs of spin as Washington Sundar is tossed the ball now.

SIX! Clean as a whistle! Reddy bowls the change up as he takes pace off but gets the length wrong. Serves it right in the slot, on off, Litton Das sets himself deep in the crease and tonks it over long on for a biggie. The six off the last ball spoils what was turning out to be a tidy over from Reddy. Ends up going for 9 runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Litton Das, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a back of a length, outside off, Litton Das walks across his stumps and swipes across the line. Gets a good connection but picks out the man at mid-wicket on the ring.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling in, on a back of a length, over middle, Litton Das hangs back and jabs it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good effort in the deep! Short and wide on off, there to be put away, Litton Das reaches out but does not quite get hold of it. Gets it off the bottom part of the bat towards deep point where Rinku Singh is quick to his right and puts in the dive to save a couple of runs for his side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Litton Das, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower delivery and it is fuller as well, on the pads, Najmul Hossain Shanto waits on it and flicks it past mid-wicket for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Reddy serves it on a back of a length, on middle, Najmul Hossain Shanto is unable to free his arms and pulls it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Follows up with a short-of-a-length delivery, angling in, on middle and leg, Najmul Hossain Shanto charges down the track and tucks it through square leg for a single. 9 runs and a wicket off this over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Arshdeep Singh to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Cracking shot! Two in two for the Bangladesh skipper! Arshdeep goes short and keeps it over middle, Najmul Hossain Shanto fetches the pull from over his head and rides the bounce well to pull it in front of square on the leg side for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Arshdeep Singh to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! A gift for Shanto to get off the mark! Arshdeep errs in line as he slips it on the pads, on a length, Najmul Hossain Shanto just tickles it down to the deep fine leg fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Arshdeep Singh to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: The skipper, Najmul Hossain Shanto walks out to bat at number 3 for Bangladesh!

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Arshdeep Singh has the last laugh after being hit for three boundaries in the first over and he lets Emon know with a stare. With an upright seam Arshdeep, on a back of a length, shaping away, Parvez Hossain Emon stays put and looks to drag the heave on the leg side from outside off. Gets an inside edge that crashes back into the off stump. Bangladesh are now 20/1 after 2.3 overs, needing 202 runs from 105 balls.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, OUT! b Arshdeep Singh.

Commentary.Commentary: Did that carry? No, just short! Arshdeep bowls the knuckle ball, on a back of a length, on middle, Parvez Hossain Emon gets tucked up for room as he looks to launch it over mid on. Gets hit high on the bat and it goes flat to mid on. Suryakumar Yadav dives ahead and takes it on the half-volley.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! At 133.5 kph, swinging away, on a good length, outside off, Parvez Hossain Emon swings for the hills as he looks to go across the line. The ball does not rise as he expected and goes under the bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace on now, on a back of a length, outside off, Litton Das lets the ball come to him and punches it wide of backward point. Rinku Singh at deep backward point is quick across to his right and keeps it down to two. Good cricket all around.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Litton Das, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Reddy takes pace off and bowls it on a back of a length, on the pads, Parvez Hossain Emon looks to glance it away but gets an inside edge on the pads and it rolls beside the pitch on the leg side for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Parvez Hossain Emon, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Reddy hits the bat hard at 134.1 kph, on off, Parvez Hossain Emon stands tall to smear it away in front of square on the leg side. Ends up hitting it straighter towards mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps it near the tramline on off, on a length, Litton Das reaches out and works it past backward point for another single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Reddy strays on the pads, on a good length, Parvez Hossain Emon swings to help it away with fine leg inside the circle. Picks out the man at short fine leg where a misfield allows a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Parvez Hossain Emon, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Reddy begins from over the wicket and lands it on a hard length, on off, Litton Das runs it down to deep third and gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Nitish Kumar Reddy to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Nitish Kumar Reddy to share the new ball attack!

FOUR! Down the ground again and the result is the same! Pace taken off by Arshdeep but hurls it a bit too full, on middle, Parvez Hossain Emon clears his front leg and drills it back past the non-striker, well away from mid on for the third boundary of the over. A good start for Bangladesh. 14 runs off thef first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! With an upright seam, swinging away, on a length, Parvez Hossain Emon swings through the line and lofts it back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that's a beauty! In the channel on off, on a good length and gets some late away shape, Parvez Hossain Emon fiddles at the delivery and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Chipped but Emon gets away with it! On a hard length, shaping away, on middle, Parvez Hossain Emon plays it early and well in front of his body. Luckily for him, he spoons it to the left of mid on for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Arshdeep bends his back and goes into the deck, outside off, Parvez Hossain Emon sways away from the line of the ball and lets the ball go.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Parvez Hossain Emon and Bangladesh are on their way! A hint of away shape, full and around off, Parvez Hossain Emon stays rooted in the crease and extends his hands into the shot. Carves it wide of cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, Four!
